{"id": "578be2b4-84d5-4137-88cc-72dbfa9676ae", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_dyHpbZklI2mo0t4uW7LJaj", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) controls\",\"context\":\"## [CT.EKS.PR.1] Require an Amazon EKS cluster to be configured with public access disabled to the cluster Kubernetes API server endpoint\\n\\nThis control checks whether an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) cluster endpoint disallows public access to the cluster Kubernetes API server endpoint.\\n\\n* **Control objective:** Limit network access\\n* **Implementation:** CloudFormation guard rule\\n* **Control behavior:** Proactive\\n* **Resource types:** `AWS::EKS::Cluster`\\n* **CloudFormation guard rule:**\\n CT.EKS.PR.1 rule specification\\n\\n**Details and examples**\\n\\n* For details about the PASS, FAIL, and SKIP behaviors associated with\\n this control, see the:\\n CT.EKS.PR.1 rule specification\\n* For examples of PASS and FAIL CloudFormation templates related to\\n this control, see:\\n CT.EKS.PR.1 example templates\\n\\n**Explanation**\\n\\nWhen you create a new cluster, Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) creates an endpoint for the managed Kubernetes API server, which you can use to communicate with your cluster using Kubernetes management tools, such as `kubectl`. By default, this API server endpoint is public to the internet, and access to the API server is secured using a combination of AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) along with native Kubernetes Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). Enabling private access to the Kubernetes API server ensures that all communication between your nodes and the API server stays within your VPC. You can limit the IP addresses that have access to your API server from the internet, or you can completely disallow internet access to the API server\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/controlreference/eks-rules.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Remediating exposures for Amazon EKS clusters\",\"context\":\"### The Amazon EKS cluster allows public access\\n\\nThe Amazon EKS cluster endpoint is the endpoint that you use to communicate with your cluster\u2019s Kubernetes API server.\\nBy default, this endpoint is public to the internet.\\nPublic endpoints increase your attack surface area and the risk of unauthorized access to your Kubernetes API server, potentially allowing attackers to access or modify cluster resources or access sensitive data.\\nFollowing security best practices, restrict access to your Amazon EKS cluster endpoint to only necessary IP ranges.\\n\\n###### Remediation\\n\\nTake one or more of the following actions to address this exposure:\\n\\n###### Modify endpoint access\\n\\nIn the exposure finding, open the resource. This opens the affected Amazon EKS cluster. You can configure your cluster to use private access, public access, or both.\\n\\nWith private access, Kubernetes API requests that originate within your cluster\u2019s VPC use the private VPC endpoint. With public access, Kubernetes API requests that originate from outside your cluster\u2019s VPC use the public endpoint.\\n\\n###### Modify or remove public access to the cluster\\n\\nTo modify endpoint access for an existing cluster, see Modifying cluster endpoint access in the *Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service User Guide*.\\nImplement more restrictive rules based on specific IP ranges or security groups.\\nIf limited public access is necessary, restrict access to specific CIDR block ranges or use prefix lists\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/exposure-eks-cluster.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Configuring control plane egress routing\",\"context\":\"## IAM condition key\\n\\nAmazon EKS supports the `eks:controlPlaneEgressMode` condition key. You can use this key in IAM policies or service control policies (SCPs) to control which egress mode callers can specify when they create or update clusters.\\n\\nThe condition key applies to the following actions:\\n\\n* `eks:CreateCluster`\\n* `eks:UpdateClusterConfig`\\n\\nFor example, the following SCP denies cluster creation and configuration updates unless the caller specifies `CUSTOMER_ROUTED`:\\n\\n```\\n{\\n \\\"Version\\\": \\\"2012-10-17\\\",\\n \\\"Statement\\\": [\\n {\\n \\\"Sid\\\": \\\"RequireCustomerRoutedControlPlane\\\",\\n \\\"Effect\\\": \\\"Deny\\\",\\n \\\"Action\\\": [\\n \\\"eks:CreateCluster\\\",\\n \\\"eks:UpdateClusterConfig\\\"\\n ],\\n \\\"Resource\\\": \\\"*\\\",\\n \\\"Condition\\\": {\\n \\\"StringNotEquals\\\": {\\n \\\"eks:controlPlaneEgressMode\\\": \\\"CUSTOMER_ROUTED\\\"\\n }\\n }\\n }\\n ]\\n}\\n```\\n\\nUse this policy to enforce that all new and updated clusters in your organization use the `CUSTOMER_ROUTED` egress mode\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/control-plane-egress.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Verify CIS EKS Benchmark 5.4.1 and 5.4.2 wording"}
